CarDS Lab Presentation
Target Trial Emulation Using ECG Embeddings
October 1st, 2026

Does X cause Y?

Ceteris paribus: all other things being equal

Randomization balances measured and unmeasured characteristics.

But RCTs are

  1. Costly
  2. Slow
  3. Often exclude multimorbid and underrepresented patients

What is propensity score matching?

  • Propensity scores (PS) balance only what is measured.
  • Claims record diagnoses, procedures and prescriptions consistently.
  • EHR labs, vital signs and imaging are missing for many patients, and not at random.
  • Many cardiovascular determinants of treatment and prognosis are physiological.

12-lead ECG as a substrate for cardiac physiology

  • Inexpensive and recorded routinely, for most patients.
  • AI-ECG detects LV dysfunction, structural heart disease and other latent phenotypes.
  • Foundation-model embeddings: general-purpose representations of cardiac physiology.

Question: can an ECG embedding capture confounding that structured data miss?

AimHypothesis: adding the ECG embedding to the PS ...
1. Balance
held-out characteristics		improves balance on clinical, laboratory and echocardiographic characteristics that no PS uses; a permuted-ECG placebo does not
2. Agreement
with RCT results		moves emulated hazard ratios toward each trial's own RCT result, beyond generic attenuation
3. Bias removal
known truth (plasmode)		removes part of the bias from a hidden physiological confounder, in proportion to how well the ECG encodes it

38 target trial emulations in Yale New Haven Health System EHR data

New-user, active-comparator designs; index dates 2011–2024; outcome = the trial's primary endpoint.

Emulation quality (design items only): see next slides.

Emulation quality of the 38 trials

Points = 1 per design flag (in-hospital start, run-in, baseline-therapy switch, follow-up ≥48 mo, time-zero issue) + comparator and outcome fidelity (moderate 1, poor 2). A poor item or ≥2 flags caps the tier at Moderate. Rated from trial protocols, blind to all results.

✓ = design flag present. F1 in-hospital start not mirrored · F2 responder/tolerability run-in · F3 baseline-therapy switch at randomization · F4 follow-up ≥48 mo · F5 other time-zero issue. Comparator/outcome: G good (0), M moderate (1), P poor (2; placebo proxy, hypothesis-changing substitution, or endpoint not ascertainable). Tier: 0 Excellent, 1–2 Good, 3 Moderate, ≥4 Limited; a poor item or ≥2 flags caps the tier at Moderate. Design items only, blind to results (docs/v19/QUALITY_REAUDIT.md).

Six PS specifications, each with and without the ECG

L2-penalized logistic PS; 1:1 greedy nearest-neighbour matching on the PS logit, caliper 0.2 SD. All other choices held constant across arms.

hdPS: empirical selection of the 200 code features (diagnoses, procedures, drugs, lab orders; once / sporadic / frequent) with the largest prevalence ratio between arms, added to the sparse PS. Schneeweiss S, et al. Epidemiology 2009;20:512–522.

Clinical PS: median 32 covariates per trial (range 28–37): 24 in every trial (age, sex, index year; 9 comorbidities; LVEF, SBP, DBP, heart rate, BMI, creatinine, K, Na, Hb; 3 visit counts) plus 3–10 trial-specific medication orders and extra diagnoses.

  • SMD = (meanT − meanC) / pooled SD, pooled SD before matching
  • Held-out: characteristics not in the PS being evaluated
  • Per trial: % with |SMD| < 0.1; paired sign-flip test across trials; placebo: permuted ECG
  • Primary panel (58): fixed before results; measured physiology most relevant to cardiac confounding
  • Expanded panel (~330 per trial): assembled afterwards from the literature; mostly coded items; sensitivity analysis

Emulated HR: Cox model in the matched cohort, robust variance clustered on matched pairs. Reference: published RCT HR (primary endpoint).

Distance: |Δ log HR| = |log HRemulated − log HRRCT|.

Consistency: |z| < 1.96, z = Δ / √(SEemulated² + SERCT²).

Benchmark shuffle: reassign RCT results at random among trials. If the gain is as large with wrong benchmarks, it is generic attenuation, not trial-specific agreement.

Trial-type categories were defined post hoc. The AF signal did not replicate in 5 prespecified AF trials (FRAIL-AF, LAAOS III, PROTECT AF, RAFT-AF, ACTIVE W; P1 |Δ| 0.254 → 0.199, 3/5 closer, p = 0.19; benchmark shuffle p = 0.28).
Quality groups from design items only (docs/v19/QUALITY_REAUDIT.md). RCT-DUPLICATE (Wang, JAMA 2023; post hoc): closely vs not closely emulated trials, r 0.93 vs 0.53, estimate agreement 88% vs 50%, standardized-difference agreement 88% vs 69%. Descriptive; no between-group test.

A simulation built on real patients

Real covariates, ECGs and follow-up are kept; treatment and outcome are simulated with a known true HR.

A measured confounder C is hidden from every PS. Bias = estimate − truth.

Hidden confounder C: echo LVEF, NT-proBNP, BMI or eGFR.

Cells: 107 trial × confounder combinations in 31 trials (≥300 per arm with C observed; 1 calibration failure excluded).

Confounding grid: OR per SD of C for treatment and HR per SD for the outcome, each 1.25, 1.5 or 2 (9 scenarios) plus a null.

Replicates: 50 subsamples (80%) per cell; true HR 0.80; PS refitted and re-matched each time.

Arm (demographic PS +)Role
nothing (base)reference bias
ECG, 32 PCstest
permuted ECG; 32 noise columnsplacebos
C itself (oracle)ceiling

% bias removed = 100 × (1 − Σ biasarm / Σ biasbase)

Compared with the ECG's cross-fitted partial R² for C (given demographics) in the real data.

  1. Balance. With a demographic PS, held-out characteristics with |SMD| < 0.1 rose from 51% to 57% (28/38 trials, p = 0.0002); permuted ECG: 51% → 52%. The gain shrinks as the PS gets richer (clinical PS: +1.3 points, p = 0.20).
  2. RCT agreement. Mean |Δ log HR| fell from 0.26 to 0.21 (25/38 closer, p = 0.002), but benchmark shuffle p = 0.22: mostly generic attenuation, not trial-specific. The AF signal did not replicate in 5 prespecified AF trials.
  3. Known truth. The ECG removed 14% of hidden-confounder bias (oracle 93%; placebos 0–1.5%), roughly 100 × the ECG's R² for the confounder.
  4. Comparator. CLMBR-T (structured-EHR model; exploratory) gave larger balance gains (+10.9 points at P1); ECG added +2.2 on top.

Limitations

  • One health system.
  • RCT results are imperfect benchmarks; trial-type categories were post hoc.
  • General-purpose ECG embedding: R² ≤ 0.35 for any confounder.
  • Most analyses exploratory; CLMBR-T comparison tentative.

Next steps

  • External validation: MIMIC-IV, UK Biobank.
  • Better ECG representations (task-specific, higher R² for physiology).
  • Manuscript: JAMA Cardiology submission.
